BOUNDARIES. Item 46 begins at the very top of p10 c1 (printed page 21-A) — nothing opens mid-item, so the owner of page 9 should be ending on item 45. Item 64 completes in full at the foot of p13 c2 (printed page 27-A): stem, all three numbered statements, the 'Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?' line and all four options are printed whole above the page footer, so nothing continues onto page 14 and page 14's owner should be opening on item 65. Numbers run 46..64 with no skips and no repeats. Layout: 2 items in c1 + 3 in c2 on p10; 3 + 3 on p11; 2 + 2 on p12; 2 + 2 on p13.

CROPS. All eight column crops were legible and no page had to be read from pNN.png; the whole-page images were used only to confirm structure and the c1/c2 boundary. The detected gutter moves 803-865px across these four pages (p10 850, p11 803, p12 852, p13 865), and the consequence is visible but harmless: on p10, p11, p12 and p13 the c1 crop carries the NEIGHBOUR'S ITEM NUMBERS down its right-hand margin (p10 c1 shows '48.' '49.' '50.'; p11 c1 shows a clipped '54' plus '55.' '56.'; p12 c1 shows '59.' '60.'; p13 c1 shows '63.' '64.'), and the c2 crops carry a sliver of c1's line-END letters down their left margin (isolated fragments such as 't', 's', 'l', 'd' on p11 c2). Both directions are overlap, not a slice: no line of either column is cut through, every c2 item number is also present intact at the top-left of its own c2 crop, and no c1 body text was absorbed into a c2 item or vice versa. Each was checked against the whole-page image. p11 has the leftmost gutter of the four and was checked most closely; its c2 crop retains 54., 55. and 56. in full.

TYPOGRAPHIC EMPHASIS NOT CARRIED. Item 57 prints the word 'not' in BOLD ITALIC ('which of the following would it *not* do ?'). The emphasis is load-bearing — it marks the item as a negative question — but there is no emphasis convention in this brief, so it is transcribed as plain 'not'. Flagged here so the negation is not read as an OCR artefact.

END-OF-LINE HYPHENS. None found in this band. Every hyphen transcribed is a printed hyphen internal to a word or compound ('non-debt', 'debt-servicing', 'short-term', 'non-farm', 'State-owned', 'privately-owned', 'Trade-Related', 'Indo-Sri Lanka'); each sits inside a line rather than at a line break, verified on the column crops.

PRINTED DEFECTS. None found. Every one of the 19 items has exactly four options (a)-(d), no option text is duplicated within an item, no fourth option is missing, and no stem is garbled or truncated. Item 47 in c1 of p10 and item 64 in c2 of p13 each sit below a large blank gap; both are column-balancing whitespace, not a dropped question — the numbering is continuous across them.

CHARACTERS PRESERVED. The rupee sign is transcribed as the printed glyph in item 50 (four occurrences) and item 58 statement 1. Item 58 statement 1 prints the year range with an en dash and spaces as '2004 - 05' in the source; it is transcribed with the en dash as printed. Item 53 quotes 'West Texas Intermediate' in single quotation marks and items 46, 55 and 62 use double quotation marks; all quotation marks are transcribed as straight ASCII quotes. No mathematical notation occurs anywhere in this band, so no item carries a LaTeX zone.

SUBTOPIC WARNINGS. Three items had no closely-fitting listed subtopic and use the nearest available label: item 53 ('West Texas Intermediate', a crude oil grade) is filed under Economy > Industry, Infrastructure and Services > Energy and Power Sector; item 54 (non-financial debt) under Capital Markets and Financial Instruments > Bonds and Debt Instruments, since its statements are about debt instruments rather than any listed macro concept; item 61 (public investment in agriculture) under Agriculture and Rural Economy > Rural Development Programmes, the closest listed heading for public capital formation in agriculture. A 'Capital Formation and Public Investment' subtopic under Agriculture and Rural Economy, and an 'Energy Commodities and Benchmarks' subtopic, would both fit this band better than anything currently listed.
